2609.04013.title: LLM4CKD: Large Language Models for Early Stage Chronic Kidney Disease Screening
2609.04013.paper_summary: Early screening of chronic kidney disease (CKD) is critical for timely intervention, yet most machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) approaches require labeled data and model training, limiting their use in real-world screening settings. This study evaluates the effectiveness of large language models (LLMs) for CKD screening under zero-shot and few-shot in-context learning settings and compares them with traditional ML and DL methods. We propose a framework that uses clinically selected tabular features and structured prompt templates to enable LLM-based inference without task-specific training. LLM performance is evaluated across multiple prompt styles, feature configurations, and data settings, and compared with standard ML, DL, and tabular foundation model (TFM) baselines, and existing CKD screening tools. The results show that LLMs can achieve competitive performance using only a small number of examples, often matching or outperforming traditional approaches in low-data settings. However, their performance remains model-dependent and less stable as input complexity increases. In contrast, ML, DL, and TFM models show more consistent improvement with larger training data. Overall, the findings highlight a trade-off between data efficiency and stability, suggesting that LLMs may serve as a flexible complementary approach for CKD screening when labeled data are limited.
2609.04013.paper_summary_zh: 早期篩檢慢性腎病（CKD）對於及時介入至關重要，但大多數機器學習（ML）和深度學習（DL）方法需要標記數據和模型訓練，限制了它們在現實篩檢環境中的使用。這項研究評估了大型語言模型（LLMs）在零樣本和少樣本上下文學習環境中進行CKD篩檢的有效性，並將其與傳統的ML和DL方法進行比較。我們提出了一個框架，利用臨床選擇的表格特徵和結構化提示模板，使基於LLM的推斷能夠在不進行特定任務訓練的情況下進行。LLM的性能在多種提示風格、特徵配置和數據設置中進行評估，並與標準的ML、DL和表格基礎模型（TFM）基準以及現有的CKD篩檢工具進行比較。結果顯示，LLMs在僅使用少量示例的情況下可以實現具有競爭力的性能，通常在低數據環境中與傳統方法相匹配或超越。然而，隨著輸入複雜性的增加，它們的性能仍然依賴於模型，且穩定性較差。相比之下，ML、DL和TFM模型在較大訓練數據下顯示出更一致的改進。總體而言，研究結果突顯了數據效率與穩定性之間的權衡，表明在標記數據有限的情況下，LLMs可能作為CKD篩檢的靈活補充方法。
2609.04013.author: Muhammad Ashad Kabir et.al.
